newsitem.title: USA: Group warns against oil industry meeting with DOE.
newsitem.headline: Group warns against oil industry meeting with DOE.

text.p: A U.S. consumer group on Wednesday warned Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary that a meeting she planned with oil industry executives this week to discuss the heating oil market might run afoul of antitrust laws.

"We believe that your scheduled meeting may provide a breeding ground for potential violation of the nation's antitrust laws barring conspiracies in restraint of trade," the letter said," Edwin Rothschild of Citizen Action said in an October 16 letter to O'Leary.
Rothschild, who first raised alarm last month about the threat of low heating oil stocks and a potential price shock, last week urged O'Leary to open the meeting to the public.

In her invitation last week to 20 chief executives from the industry, O'Leary said she was "most interested in your perspective concerning the factors that are affecting the availability and price volatility of winter heating fuels, how these factors may change, and steps the federal government should be prepared to take to address economic concerns created by these market circumstances."
She said she did not want to discuss proprietary issues.

"We do not intend, at this meeting, to request any specific supply or pricing action by any company or to encourage any specific cooperative activity among participating companies," O'Leary's letter said.

She also said an official from the Justice Department's antitrust division would be at the meeting, but Rothschild charged that that would not protect companies from potential attacks under antitrust laws.
Amid the latest complaint from Citizen Action, winter fuel
suppliers in New England were meeting in New Hampshire with Energy Information Administration officials to discuss the heating oil supply situation.
The American Petroleum Institute reported Tuesday that distillate stocks, which include heating oil, at the end of last week were 17.7 million barrels lower than a year ago.
